scripts.verify: pnpm check:eol && pnpm format:check && turbo run typecheck && turbo run lint && turbo run test && pnpm policy:test && pnpm tasks:check
scripts.dev:reset: docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d --wait
scripts.dev:psql: docker exec -it yourtal-postgres psql -U yourtal -d yourtal
scripts.dev:fresh: pnpm dev:reset && pnpm db:migrate && pnpm db:seed && pnpm media:publish
scripts.//verify: The repo gate. It runs the line-ending guard, typecheck (incl. `go vet`), lint, every test suite, the Cerbos policy suite and the task-board staleness check. Each clause was added because it was OUTSIDE the gate and something broke there unseen: Go had no package.json so `turbo run test` ran 0 of 23 Go test files; lint was red in @yourtal/db while verify passed; the 384 policy tests ran only by hand. --concurrency=1 USED TO be required here — @yourtal/db, @yourtal/api and @yourtal/idempotency all wrote to the one real 'yourtal' database, so running their test tasks at the same time corrupted each other's rows regardless of any single package's own fileParallelism setting. YT-0547 gave each of those three its own database, created and dropped by `packages/db/scripts/with-test-db.mjs` before/after its package's own `vitest` run, so the workspace gate no longer needs to serialise them — proved by running them concurrently, not assumed (see that ticket's report). services/ledger and services/voucher's `go test` still talk to the real 'yourtal' directly, on their own roles with disjoint schema grants (ledger vs voucher), which is why running the two of them alongside everything else did not reproduce the old failure in verification. check:eol is first because it is the cheapest and because a CRLF shell script fails on the Linux host rather than here. format:check was added after the first CI run ever executed found 9 files drifted — `format.yml` had existed the whole time and had never run.
